terms.definition: One unit of work on the board. A card has a status, labels, a devlog and a gate verdict.
The list of cards for every project, shown in Work and served at /api/backlog.
One of the four top-level views: Surface, Learning, Work and Wiki.
One run of a coding agent, captured from the logs the agent already writes.
A scheduled or event-driven job the kernel owns, with a maker, an independent checker and a ceiling.
A durable promise a loop opens and closes, so a missed job shows as overdue instead of silently not happening.
The GLMPS server process. In production it runs as the GLMPS2 Windows service.
Where GLMPS keeps everything it writes: the board, loop records, wiki builds and logs. Not the repository.
The verification verdict recorded on a card: PASS, CONCERNS, FAIL or WAIVED, with evidence and a risk level.
The progress notes on a card. Each one is relayed into the card's Slack thread.
The server-side path a pull request takes to main: tests, an independent review against the acceptance criteria, then the merge.
The queue runner. It launches queued cards as agent sessions, each in its own git worktree.
A voice or text conversation with several specialist agents taking turns on one floor.
Moving merged work onto the live service: a fast-forward of the runtime checkout and a service restart.
